1.stem: [Academic Talk — Ecology] What did the seedling survey conducted five years after the cyclone show?

options.A: Nearly all the new seedlings were clustered along the debris lines the cyclone left
options.B: Seedlings were coming up mainly beneath the surviving adult trees
options.C: Seedlings were scarce across the island despite a heavy fruit crop
options.D: Seedlings were plentiful at first, but few survived their first dry season

2.stem: [Academic Talk — Archaeology] What did the professor say the sediment cores indicated about rainfall in the settlement's final decades?

options.A: That rainfall rose noticeably compared with earlier centuries
options.B: That rainfall stayed close to the region's long-term average
options.C: That rainfall declined gradually across those decades
options.D: That rainfall swung between unusually wet and unusually dry years

3.stem: [Academic Talk — Linguistics] Why does the professor discuss the 1911 field recordings?

options.A: They establish that the shift was already finished a century ago
options.B: They preserve the speech of a village that the shift never reached
options.C: They catch speakers in mid-shift, using the older and newer vowels side by side
options.D: They show why transcriptions from that period cannot be trusted on vowel quality

4.stem: [Academic Talk — Linguistics] What does the professor say the vocabulary shared by Taruic and Emel indicates about the vowel shift?

options.A: The shift was already complete when the words were borrowed
options.B: The borrowing ran in the other direction, from Emel into Taruic
options.C: The words were borrowed twice, at two different stages of the shift
options.D: The shift happened after the borrowing, since Emel preserves the older vowels

5.stem: [Academic Talk — Art History] What did the professor say the pigment analysis revealed about the blue areas of the Verrine Hours?

options.A: The blue is mostly indigo, blended to imitate the look of lapis lazuli
options.B: Lapis lazuli was used throughout, even in the minor border decoration
options.C: A cheaper azurite base was covered with a thin layer of lapis lazuli
options.D: Azurite appears in the margins, while lapis lazuli was reserved for the central figures

6.stem: [Academic Talk — Linguistics] What is the professor's central claim about how the vowel shift spread?

options.A: It took hold first in careful, formal speech and reached casual speech later
options.B: It traveled along the river trade routes rather than spreading outward from one center
options.C: It was carried by younger speakers whose parents never adopted the new vowels
options.D: It moved through the vocabulary word by word rather than reaching all words at once

7.stem: [Academic Talk — Art History] Why does the professor bring up the workshop's surviving account books?

options.A: They narrow the book's production to a two-year window
options.B: They show the patron stopped paying partway through, which explains the unfinished pages
options.C: They list the assistants by name, showing how many people worked on a single book
options.D: They record what the workshop paid for pigments, giving evidence independent of the analysis

8.stem: [Academic Talk — Volcanology] According to the professor, what did the gas measurements suggest about the source of the unrest?

options.A: Fresh magma was rising and stalling beneath the caldera
options.B: Heated groundwater, rather than new magma, was driving the changes
options.C: Gas from an older, cooling intrusion was escaping along reopened faults
options.D: The gases carried the signature of magma and groundwater together, pointing to a mixed source

9.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Science] According to the professor, why did the service's warnings improve in its second decade?

options.A: The service began paying fishing crews to report conditions from open water
options.B: Telegraph lines finally connected the coastal observation stations
options.C: It began pooling its observations with the rival Austrian service
options.D: It replaced its old seasonal rules of thumb with warnings based on barometer readings

10.stem: [Academic Talk — Art History] What does the professor conclude about attributing the Verrine Hours to Master Anselm himself?

options.A: He probably painted the faces, while assistants completed the rest
options.B: The attribution holds, because the underdrawing throughout is in his hand
options.C: The strongest pages were painted after his documented death, so the attribution fails
options.D: The attribution holds, on the strength of the page layouts and borders rather than the figures

11.stem: [Academic Talk — Volcanology] What does the professor say the ground-deformation measurements showed during the unrest episode at the Serrat caldera?

options.A: The deformation covered a much smaller area than the first reports claimed
options.B: The uplift was centered under the caldera's western rim rather than its middle
options.C: The ground rose and then subsided again in a repeating cycle
options.D: The uplift went on steadily even after the earthquake swarms had stopped

12.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Science] What is the professor's judgment of Marini, the service's founder?

options.A: A man of ordinary ideas whose real achievement was the organization he built
options.B: A reckless forecaster whose premature warnings wore down public trust
options.C: A gifted promoter whose scientific claims ran ahead of his evidence
options.D: An undervalued figure whose statistical methods anticipated later practice

13.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Science] What does the professor imply about the service's barometer records today?

options.A: Recent recalibration work suggests their readings ran consistently low
options.B: They have become a resource for reconstructing the region's past climate
options.C: Most of them did not survive, so claims about the service's accuracy cannot be checked
options.D: They sit scattered in regional archives and remain largely unstudied

14.stem: [Academic Talk — Archaeology] Why does the professor mention the neighboring settlement of Kessara?

options.A: Its excavation used newer methods that the professor wants applied at Tell Arvani
options.B: It was abandoned around the same time, which points to a cause beyond a single site
options.C: It continued to function afterward, which complicates a region-wide explanation
options.D: Its tablets refer to Tell Arvani, which helps date the final occupation layer

15.stem: [Academic Talk — Archaeology] What is the professor's assessment of the earthquake explanation for the abandonment of Tell Arvani?

options.A: It may account for some of the damage, but not for the abandonment by itself
options.B: The damage pattern fits an earthquake, but one that struck centuries before the abandonment
options.C: The collapsed walls support it, and it is currently the best-supported explanation
options.D: It rests on damage that turned out to reflect gradual decay rather than a single event

16.stem: [Academic Talk — Art History] What is the main point the professor makes about the workshop that produced the Verrine Hours?

options.A: It reused compositions from an older model book for decades
options.B: Its books have long been confused with the output of a rival workshop in Arden
options.C: Its choices of material followed each patron's budget more than any artistic rule
options.D: It kept working in an older style long after painters elsewhere had moved on

17.stem: [Academic Talk — Ecology] Why does the professor refer to the kanari forests on the mainland?

options.A: To show that the change was confined to the atoll rather than affecting the species as a whole
options.B: To question whether conclusions drawn from mainland forests apply to an atoll at all
options.C: To identify where replacement pigeons might eventually come from
options.D: To point out that the tree spreads there without pigeons, so other dispersers can do the job

18.stem: [Academic Talk — Linguistics] How does the professor evaluate the substrate explanation for the shift?

options.A: Recently revived, and in the professor's view it has earned a fresh hearing
options.B: Well supported, because loanwords show the earlier language had these same vowels
options.C: Appealing, but impossible to confirm without records of the earlier language
options.D: Unconvincing, because the shift's geography does not match where the substrate was spoken

19.stem: [Academic Talk — Archaeology] According to the professor, what did the residue analysis show the large storage jars had mostly held?

options.A: Dried fish carried up from the coast
options.B: Barley grown in the fields around the settlement
options.C: Wine brought in from outside the region
options.D: Olive oil pressed at the settlement itself

20.stem: [Academic Talk — Volcanology] What does the professor imply about the decision to raise the alert level partway through the episode?

options.A: It followed a fixed protocol that left the scientists themselves little say
options.B: It came later than the data warranted, in the professor's reading
options.C: It was justified at the time, given what the instruments were then showing
options.D: It was driven more by public pressure than by the monitoring data

21.stem: [Academic Talk — Volcanology] Why does the professor bring up the caldera's nineteenth-century episode?

options.A: It was misread by observers at the time in a way the professor thinks is being repeated
options.B: It ended without an eruption, showing that unrest at this caldera does not always lead to one
options.C: Its opening phase resembled the recent unrest, which is why the recent episode drew such attention
options.D: It left the deposits that let geologists map how far the hazard zone extends

22.stem: [Academic Talk — Ecology] What does the professor suggest about intervening to move seeds by hand?

options.A: The research team is against it, since it would obscure how the system recovers on its own
options.B: A proposal to bring pigeons from a neighboring atoll is being weighed instead
options.C: A small trial of it is already underway on the island's two worst-hit stretches
options.D: Managers are holding off because pigeon numbers have begun to recover

23.stem: [Academic Talk — Ecology] According to the professor, what did the follow-up experiment indicate about why seed dispersal changed?

options.A: The fruit was ripening out of step with the pigeons' breeding season, so fewer birds fed on it
options.B: Rats were removing most of the fallen fruit before the pigeons could reach it
options.C: The pigeon flocks had grown too small to take the fruit before it dropped and spoiled
options.D: A vine that spread after the storm was covering the branches the pigeons feed from

24.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Science] Why does the professor describe the shipwreck of 1873?

options.A: It pushed the parliament into funding the warning network
options.B: It occurred despite an accurate warning, showing that warnings were not reaching crews
options.C: It illustrates what storms were costing the coast before systematic warnings
options.D: It was wrongly blamed on the service and nearly ended the project
